title: Regular alteration adapted to nested opens and a prescribed finite cover
statement:
Let $k$ be any field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $T$ be a nonempty integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $S\subseteq T^\circ\subseteq T$ be dense open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $c:H\to S$ be a nonempty connected finite etale surjection [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. There exist a regular integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ [def-weil-regular-scheme], a proper dominant generically finite $h:Y\to T$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], and a reduced strict normal crossings boundary $D=\bigcup_{a\in A}D_a$ in $Y$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], with $A$ finite, such that
$$W:=h^{-1}(S)=Y\setminus D,\qquad V:=h^{-1}(T^\circ)=Y\setminus\bigcup_{a\in A_{\rm out}}D_a$$
for some $A_{\rm out}\subseteq A$. Here generically finite means that $k(Y)/k(T)$ is finite. The proper surjection $r:W\to S$ induced by $h$ factors through $c:H\to S$. Moreover, there is a nonempty dense open $S_0\subseteq S$ such that $r_0:W_0=W\times_S S_0\to S_0$ is finite and factors as
$$W_0\xrightarrow{u}T_0\xrightarrow{e}S_0,$$
where $u$ is a finite universal homeomorphism (a finite map that is a homeomorphism after every scheme base change) and $e$ is finite etale surjective of a constant degree $d\geq1$. Empty boundaries and $S=T^\circ=T$ are allowed. No strict normal crossings assertion is made for the complement of $W_0$ in $Y$, and no separability of $k(Y)/k(T)$ is asserted.

source.place: Agent-formulated geometric consequence of X Theorem 2.1, printed p.149 (global projective alteration with regular source and SNC boundary), with separate blowups of the two boundary ideals before applying the theorem; IX Theorem 1.1, p.131, is only local uniformization and is not alone a proper alteration theorem. Compactify a component of H over T, then apply X 2.1. Generic finite radicial/etale factorization is obtained after shrinking from the maximal separable subextension of k(Y)/k(T).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-cover-nested-cartier-preparation] to $T,S,T^\circ,c$. Choose a point of the nonempty generic cover fibre as in that lemma. Obtain $g:B\to T$, integral separated finite-type $B$, and effective Cartier ideals $\mathcal I_B,\mathcal J_B$ with supports $B\setminus g^{-1}S$ and $B\setminus g^{-1}T^\circ$. The lemma gives $g$ proper dominant with $k(B)/k(T)$ finite and a factorization $g^{-1}S\to H\to S$. Since $S\subseteq T^\circ$, the second support is contained in the first.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-alteration-cartier-subboundary] to $B,\mathcal I_B,\mathcal J_B$, giving $a:Y\to B$, $D=\bigcup_{i\in A}D_i$ and $A_{\rm out}$. Set $h=ga$. Proper composition makes $h$ proper. Its induced function-field inclusion is the composite $k(T)\subseteq k(B)\subseteq k(Y)$, hence it is dominant and finite (multiply finite field bases). The two support identities of the lemma give $h^{-1}S=Y\setminus D$ and $h^{-1}T^\circ=Y\setminus\bigcup_{i\in A_{\rm out}}D_i$. All regularity, integrality, separatedness and finite-type assertions on $Y$ are supplied by that lemma. In Lean, the finite divisor family is identified with all irreducible components of the boundary support: each divisor is integral and closed, its generic point has ambient local dimension one by the singleton intersection formula, and hence no distinct divisor support contains another. A finite irreducible closed cover with this antichain property enumerates exactly the maximal irreducible subsets.

source.place: X Theorem 2.1, printed p.149, and VIII Remark 4.2.2(i); integral-component selection followed by local Cartier-subboundary factorization. The latter uses literature/stacks-project/more-algebra.tex, Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD). Agent consequence comprising the returned parent proof, original steps 3--4, whose complete argument is retained in the theorem docstring.

proof.text: Put $W=h^{-1}S$. Proper base change makes $r:W\to S$ proper. The image of $h$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] and contains the generic point, so it is all of $T$; thus $r$ is surjective and $W$ is nonempty. The map $W\to g^{-1}S\to H$ supplies the required factorization through $c$. The nonempty open $W$ in integral $Y$ is integral with the same function field: its generic point and its local ring are unchanged. It is separated finite type over $k$, as is the open $S$ in the Noetherian finite-type scheme $T$. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-generic-radicial-etale-factorization] to $r$, whose function-field extension is the finite extension $k(Y)/k(T)$. Its $S_0,T_0,u,e,d$ are exactly the required final data. The earlier two support identities are retained; no boundary claim is made after shrinking to $S_0$. For the final constant degree, use local constancy of the finite etale rank on the nonempty integral open S_0: choose d to be its value at the generic point. Surjectivity gives d>=1. Thus no comparison with the auxiliary sheaf-rank witness is needed.
